questions.q: Why is the Indian Constitution called a living document?
answer: The Indian Constitution is called a living document because, like a living being, it is able to grow and adapt to changing circumstances rather than remaining fixed and lifeless.

answer.text: Its makers gave it a careful balance between rigidity and flexibility. Its core values are protected, yet it can be amended to meet new needs. Under Article 368 it can be changed by different procedures, and over a hundred amendments have already been made, showing how responsive it is.

The Constitution also evolves through the interpretation of the courts, which read its provisions in the light of new situations. At the same time, the Supreme Court's basic structure doctrine ensures that amendments cannot destroy its essential features.
The working of institutions and the pressure of public opinion further shape its meaning.

answer: Because it keeps adapting while preserving its spirit, the Constitution remains a living document.
